decisions.reason: Each utterance states, in the first person, difficulty or discomfort in breathing: at rest (indices 141, 144, 148), on a short walk or a light activity (140, 143, 145, 147, 149) or while talking (142, 146). The two descriptions differ only by “subjetiva”.
Dispneia fits, but the utterance states the seated position and nothing excludes the un-keyed entry Platipneia (B025-01).

Each utterance states that breathlessness starts while the trunk or body is bent or inclined forward (to reach a foot, a low cabinet, the floor, a backpack by the feet, a boot, under a table). Eight also state relief on straightening (150–155, 158, 159); the source description does not require it. The words “para a frente” are literal in 152 and 159; in the others the direction is stated by the gesture (B025-05).
Breathlessness on bending is itself difficulty in breathing; same umbrella convention as the base Ortopneia and Trepopneia stories and the batch's Platipneia stories (B025-03).
“Sentada à mesa…” states a posture named in the description; no comparison with lying down is given, and nothing excludes the entry (B025-01).
“Parada” states stillness; no posture is named and no comparison with lying down is made (B025-02).
Breathlessness starts on bending, not on sitting or standing; 155 states that seated breathing is fine, 153 that standing erect relieves. No utterance compares with lying down.

findings.issue: Index 141: “Sentada à mesa fazendo um desenho, percebo que respirar está desconfortável. A sensação é de que o ar nunca é suficiente.” The story keys the two Dispneia entries only. findings.resolution: Reviewer agrees with the key on these points. No utterance mentions the nose, so the breathing difficulty of Obstrução nasal (read with its label) is not described. In every utterance the limit is stated as breathing, not movement, strength, pain, fear, noise or heartbeat. No utterance mentions lying down, a side, or waking from sleep. The only positional doubt is index 141 (B025-01).

findings.issue: Index 144: “Faço uma inspiração” is slightly technical for a patient. Index 145: “dobrava toalhas” uses the verb that the Flexopneia stories use for the trunk (“dobro o corpo”); the object is the towels and no bending is stated. Index 150: “Ao levantar o tronco, consigo respirar melhor” echoes the Ortopneia description (“melhorar ao sentar ou elevar o tronco”), with no lying down. Indices 151, 154 and 158 state that the body or trunk is inclined (“me inclinar … no armário baixo”, “fiquei inclinada” reaching the floor, “inclino o tronco para fechar o zíper da bota”) without the words “para a frente”; the direction follows from the task. Indices 152, 158 and 159 use the source's own words (“para a frente”, “inclino o tronco”, “falta ar”) as the clue.
findings.resolution: None of these opens another term. For 151, 154 and 158 the reviewer considers the forward direction stated by ordinary meaning (one bends forward to reach a low cabinet, the floor or a boot) and no other entry concerns inclination of the trunk; a teacher who wants the direction said in words can ask for “para a frente” to be added. Suggested polish for a later edit: 144 “Respiro fundo e ainda parece faltar”; 145 another light task (for example, setting the table).

findings.issue: The ten cardiovascular Dispneia stories reuse the scenario set of the ten LARINGE/FARINGE Dispneia stories of the same batch (indices 60–69, outside this scope), which key the same two contexts: seated at a table (141 / 60), short walk that used to be easy (140, 149 / 61), pauses in conversation with the voice explicitly spared (142 / 62), light household task (145 / 63), slowing down in a short walk (143 / 66), standing still (144, 148 / 68), bath (147 / 69).

findings.issue: Story-level rationales are specific to each utterance and name only Dispneia and Flexopneia. In 140–149 the LARINGE/FARINGE evidence rationale is one stock sentence with a missing full stop: “O relato explicita a manifestação definida em Dispneia: sensação subjetiva de diﬁculdade ou desconforto para respirar A posição no roteiro não define etiologia.”. In 150–159 the two Dispneia evidence rationales are stock sentences with the same defect: “A fala documenta os critérios da entrada Dispneia: sensação subjetiva de diﬁculdade ou desconforto para respirar A hierarquia localiza o item sem comprovar etiologia.”. Index 142 mentions “perda vocal” and index 146 “alteração vocal”, both to exclude a voice complaint, as the utterances themselves do. Index 154's rationale says “flexão anterior” where the utterance says “inclinada”.
findings.resolution: No rationale names another symptom as the finding, describes a different sentence or carries a wrong gender; there is no copy-paste leftover from another group. The missing full stop should be fixed in a later edit if the evidence rationale is ever shown to students.

supportedAcceptedPaths.terminologyCaution: A apostila descreve Flexopneia como “falta de ar ao inclinar o tronco para frente.” (na literatura em inglês, bendopnea). A descrição impressa não fixa tempo de início nem exige alívio ao endireitar. A entrada está em APARELHO CARDIOVASCULAR, mas a fala isolada não estabelece insuficiência cardíaca nem outra causa. Reconhecimento descritivo e fonte-específico.
supportedAcceptedPaths.rationale: A fala relata falta de ar, ar curto ou dificuldade para respirar que aparece quando a pessoa inclina, curva ou dobra o tronco para a frente: corresponde a “falta de ar ao inclinar o tronco para frente.”. A rubrica APARELHO CARDIOVASCULAR apenas localiza a entrada.

items.reasoning: Para olhar debaixo da mesa a pessoa dobra “o corpo para a frente” e “logo” sente que falta ar; volta o tronco para respirar melhor. Flexão à frente dita literalmente, falta de ar imediata e alívio ao desfazer a posição: Flexopneia pela descrição impressa. Dispneia (duas entradas) sustentada pela falta de ar. Palavras da fonte como pista fácil (B025-05). A justificativa corresponde à fala e não atribui causa.

contextDistinctions.printedPlacement: APARELHO CARDIOVASCULAR (Flexopneia, Dispneia) and APARELHO RESPIRATÓRIO (LARINGE/FARINGE) (Dispneia), no printed subgroup, are the actual source placements of the keyed entries; the headings locate the entries and are not evidence of cardiac, laryngeal or pharyngeal disease.
contextDistinctions.clinicalMeaning: Subjectively reported breathlessness that comes on while the trunk is bent forward. No cause established; the utterance alone does not establish heart failure.
contextDistinctions.unmentionedInformation: Unmentioned clinical facts remain unknown, not absent.
contextDistinctions.otherPaths: Ortopneia, Platipneia, Trepopneia e Dispneia paroxística noturna não: sem deitar, sem comparação com deitar, sem lado, sem sono. Tontura não relatada. Dor (peito) e Palpitação não descritas.

alternativeAssessment.rule: +5 only for an evidenced valid subgroup in another context for the same concept; equally supported complete paths receive full credit.
alternativeAssessment.result: Three keyed paths (Flexopneia; Dispneia in LARINGE/FARINGE and in APARELHO CARDIOVASCULAR) are accepted with full credit: breathlessness on bending the trunk forward is stated, and breathlessness is itself the broad entry Dispneia (base convention for Ortopneia and Trepopneia). Ortopneia, Platipneia, Trepopneia and Dispneia paroxística noturna are not supported: no lying down, no relief on lying, no side, no sleep. No partial-credit subgroup identified.
